name: Leiden University
summary: Research university in Leiden with a second campus in The Hague; 17 English-taught bachelor's, from Security Studies to Data Science and AI.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma required (not certificates); send grade 11, November grade 12 and predicted grades. English-taught IB or English A HL waives the English test. Science programmes set HL subjects.

programmes.name: African Studies
programmes.about: Africa's history, languages, literature and societies studied across the humanities; you learn Swahili and spend a semester of year two studying in an African country.
programmes.overview: You study Africa from an Africa-centred perspective, combining history, linguistics with Swahili language learning, anthropology, literature and cultural studies, area studies and sociology, with attention to ethnicity, gender and socio-economic background. In your second year you spend a semester in an African country for language immersion and courses at a local university. You learn to build and use databases and visual research tools, and to produce documentaries, podcasts and blogs. You can shape the degree around a discipline, a theme, the continent or a particular region, and draw on the African Studies Centre Leiden and its specialist library.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Archaeology
programmes.about: How past societies lived, reconstructed from material remains, with theory in class and hands-on fieldwork; Leiden's large archaeology faculty lets you specialise by region and period.
programmes.overview: The programme covers past societies, cultures and human behaviour, combining archaeological theory with practice and a broad view of the discipline. You take part in national and international fieldwork, work in laboratory practicals and join the research projects of staff. Contemporary issues such as migration, globalisation and climate change are seen through an archaeological lens, and you can focus on heritage in society, including policy and the heritage of migrant communities. Graduates find work in fields such as heritage management and museums, or continue to a master.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Arts, Media and Society
programmes.about: Contemporary visual art, from painting and photography to installation, performance and digital media, and how art connects with society, media and issues such as climate and conflict.
programmes.overview: You study modern and contemporary visual art forms, from painting, photography and installation art to video art, bio-art, games, performance and digital media art, and how art relates to society and to the role of media in that relationship. The programme also links art to fields such as science and politics, and brings in sociology, cultural representation, cinema and contemporary media studies. You gain hands-on experience through research projects, field trips to museums, galleries and media institutions, and guest lectures by artists, scholars and scientists. Leiden gives easy access to museums and galleries in The Hague, Amsterdam and Rotterdam, and the degree prepares you for academia or the public or private sector.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
programmes.about: Why people live and think differently across the world, studied through theory plus your own fieldwork, internships and ethnographic film-making, with themes like inequality and climate justice.
programmes.overview: Four themes run through the programme: sustainability, diversity, digitalisation and methodology. Topics range from climate change and low-carbon futures to social media use, gender, racism, LGBTQIA+ rights, homelessness, food habits and child labour. You do fieldwork in the Netherlands and abroad, internships with organisations and communities, and use creative research methods such as photography, film, zine-making and drawing. Lectures and seminars give the theory, and the degree prepares you to support individuals, groups and communities affected by pressing social issues.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
programmes.about: Computer science, maths, statistics and machine learning combined, building strong programming foundations and AI skills, taught at Leiden's computer science institute (LIACS).
programmes.overview: You build a foundation in computer science and computational thinking, mathematics and statistics, programming, algorithms and information processing, and apply it to machine learning, cognitive science and artificial intelligence. Teaching is directly inspired by current research, and you can take part in research projects. The degree is run by LIACS, the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science, and trains you as a computer scientist able to develop AI systems.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Dutch Studies
programmes.ib: Taught in English and Dutch, for international students; open from absolute beginner in Dutch to advanced.
programmes.about: Dutch language, literature, history and society for international students, starting from any level of Dutch; classes are taught partly in Dutch from the first semester.
programmes.overview: You study the Dutch language, from beginner to advanced level, together with Dutch culture, history, society and ways of thinking. Classes are in Dutch from the first semester, so you learn through immersion and alongside Dutch students, in the historic city of Leiden, an international centre of Dutch studies. A one-year option combines language modules with electives such as Dutch Painting and Dutch Debates. Graduates can teach Dutch, work for international organisations connected to the Netherlands, or continue to a master focused on Dutch language or culture.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: English Language and Culture
programmes.about: English in all its forms, from medieval texts to contemporary literature, film and linguistics, alongside advanced training in your own written and spoken English.
programmes.overview: You study the structure and acquisition of English, literature from Shakespeare to contemporary authors, the culture of Britain and other English-speaking countries, and Old and Middle English texts in the original, while building advanced spoken and written English. Language change is linked to societal change over time. Teaching is in English with a personal approach between students and lecturers, and specialisation courses in years two and three let you tailor the programme. Year three can include a minor, an internship or study abroad. Graduates move into academic careers, the public and private sectors, or media and cultural institutions such as film festivals, or continue to a master in literary studies.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: International Studies
programmes.about: One of eight world regions studied through its history, politics, economics and culture, while you learn a major language of that region; taught in The Hague.
programmes.overview: You approach global developments through history, politics, economics and culture, with lectures from several disciplines and language study tied to your region. You choose one of eight regional specialisations: Africa, East Asia, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East, North America, Russia and Eurasia, or South Asia and Southeast Asia, each with its own language options. In year three the PRINS course is a 12-week consultancy project in which teams tackle real challenges for organisations such as UN agencies, War Child Alliance and the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The programme is based in The Hague, seat of the Dutch government, and prepares you for academia or the public or private sector.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Liberal Arts and Sciences: Global Challenges (Leiden University College)
programmes.ib: Selective: 35 IB points incl. bonus to enter selection, any maths at 4 advised (2026-27 list). Early bird 1 Dec 2026; final 15 Mar 2027. Five majors.
programmes.about: Global challenges such as peace, justice, sustainability and development, studied in small interdisciplinary classes on a residential campus in The Hague before you pick a major.
programmes.overview: Global challenges such as climate change, conflict and inequality organise the programme, and you look at them through several disciplines before specialising, learning to see connections between fields. Classes are small and interactive, averaging about 18 students, with plenty of discussion and debate. You then major in one of five areas: Culture, History and Society; Earth, Energy and Sustainability; Governance, Economics and Development; International Justice; or World Politics. The college is in The Hague, with its ministries, international organisations and NGOs close by for professional contacts.
programmes.selectionNote: Holistic review, in order: academics, English, motivation, activities, maths; plus an online pre-admission class and written reflection. Early bird 1 Dec, final 15 Mar.

programmes.name: Linguistics
programmes.about: How languages are built, compared and change, including endangered languages, with specialisations such as descriptive and comparative Indo-European linguistics. No other languages needed.
programmes.overview: You learn how language works: sound systems and syntax, how children acquire language, how languages compare, how endangered languages are documented and how languages change over time. Teaching happens in small classes with regular contact with teachers, and experimental work uses four language labs: Babylab, EEG, phonetics and eye-tracking. In year two you choose a specialisation: Descriptive Linguistics, Language and Cognition, Comparative Indo-European Linguistics, or the Dutch-taught Language in Use. The research behind the field feeds practical applications such as help for speech disorders, language software and preserving endangered languages.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Philosophy: Global and Comparative Perspectives
programmes.about: Philosophy's big questions studied by comparing Western thought with Indian, East Asian, African and Arabic traditions side by side, rather than as separate options.
programmes.overview: You explore questions about reality, the mind and society through philosophical traditions from China, India, East Asia, Africa and the Arab world as well as Western philosophy from antiquity to the present, including ethics taught in tutorial seminars. Teaching centres on small tutorial groups for in-depth discussion, lectures by internationally known scholars, skills training and mentoring by senior students. You can tailor the curriculum to your interests, use the Asian Library collections, and add a semester abroad or an international internship. The training in critical thinking and handling complex information suits many employers, and a master such as Modern European Philosophy is an option.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Political Science: International Relations and Organisations
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 Jan 2027, grade average by 31 Jan, online assessment 18-19 Feb. Maths to graduation, including probability and statistics.
programmes.about: Diplomacy, conflict, international institutions and transnational problems studied as political science, in The Hague among UN bodies, embassies and NGOs.
programmes.overview: You study global affairs and diplomacy, with courses such as Introduction to International Organisations, International Security and Introduction to International Relations, plus academic skills. Themes include conflict resolution, terrorism, peace and security, poverty, refugee crises, humanitarian cooperation, nuclear weapons reduction and globalisation, with a focus on major powers such as China, Russia, the USA and the EU and on bodies such as the UN, NATO, the IMF and the World Bank. You develop research, writing and presentation skills and write a thesis. The programme is based in The Hague, a UN city with many international organisations, embassies and NGOs.

needs.note: Maths taken to graduation, with probability and statistics.

programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: ranked on your school grade average (due 31 Jan) and an online assessment on 18-19 Feb 2027; ranking number by 15 April.

programmes.name: Psychology (International Bachelor in Psychology)
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus, 600 places (Dutch and English tracks): apply by 15 Jan 2027; ranked on grade average, an online assessment and a draw (2027-28 criteria). Maths to graduation.
programmes.about: Psychology as a science, from brain and cognition to social, clinical and developmental psychology, with research methods and statistics throughout; the English track of Leiden's psychology bachelor.
programmes.overview: The programme gives a broad overview of the sub-areas of psychology, beginning with foundations such as bio-neuropsychology, which covers brain anatomy and how internal processes shape behaviour and psychological disorders. Lectures are interactive and often given by several specialists, and work groups use case examples from clinical practice and video analysis of real situations such as neuropsychological assessments. Halfway through you choose three specialisation courses in the areas that interest you. Studying in English also builds communication and cross-cultural collaboration skills.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: four groups by grade average (7.5 line) and a pass on the online assessment; a draw ranks you within your group. 600 places shared with the Dutch track.

programmes.name: Science for Sustainable Societies
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL, plus one HL and one SL from Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Economics, Geography or ESS.
programmes.about: Sustainability problems tackled across natural science, social science and governance, with practical skills such as coding, GIS and working with stakeholders.
programmes.overview: The programme rests on three pillars: planet, with environmental biology, industrial ecology, earth system science and ecological modelling; people, with anthropology, environmental psychology and human-environment relationships; and politics, with environmental governance, policy mechanisms and social transition. Large lectures are combined with small discussion seminars, and learning is project-based, with fieldwork, site visits to see environmental impacts, hands-on assignments and living labs. You gain skills in project management, programming, modelling and GIS, preparing you to contribute to the sustainability sector.

needs.note: A second, different subject from the same list.

programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Security Studies
programmes.about: Terrorism, cybercrime, crises and conflict studied in their political, historical and social context, with a practical focus on how governments and organisations respond; taught in The Hague.
programmes.overview: You study security through political science, law, economics and history, using cases such as Syria, terrorism and counterterrorism, the Fukushima disaster, the SARS epidemic and the role of media, with attention to crisis management and governance. Teaching follows an Explore, Understand, Do approach, with lectures paired with skills labs in small groups, case studies that bring in current events, and academic and professional skills training. The programme is in The Hague, known as a city of peace, justice and security, and combines research with a practical orientation.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: South and Southeast Asian Studies
programmes.about: The history, cultures and politics of South and Southeast Asia, studied alongside a language of the region: Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian.
programmes.overview: You study the history, cultures and politics of South and Southeast Asia, including development and inequality, ethnic and religious conflict, political and cultural movements and the tension between modernity and tradition, and learn one language: Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian. You specialise in either modern societies or classical cultures, with lectures, seminars and language classes. In the third year you spend a semester in the region, at Gadjah Mada University in Yogyakarta, the University of Hyderabad or the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in Kathmandu depending on your language, and write a BA dissertation.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

programmes.name: Urban Studies
programmes.about: Cities and their problems, such as sustainability, diversity, safety and health, studied across the humanities, social sciences, science and law, using The Hague as the case.
programmes.overview: Four themes structure the degree: the sustainable city, the multicultural city, the safe city and the healthy city, set against theories of urban development, the history of cities and future urban trends. You learn in the classroom and in actual urban environments, on field trips to Dutch cities, through individual and group research projects, and in methods courses on observation, interviews, social network analysis and spatial analysis. In year two you specialise in one of the four themes, and year three offers an internship, exchange or minor, then a research lab with your thesis. Graduates move into academia, business or the public sector, or into a research or technical master.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; online matching is compulsory, its advice not binding.

notes: Every programme without a numerus fixus has compulsory matching; for Security Studies it opens in February 2027 and must be finished before 1 August 2027.
Leiden University College guarantees first-years a furnished studio on its The Hague campus; Leiden's other rooms are first come, first served and not guaranteed.
Binding study advice: you must earn at least 45 of the 60 first-year credits to continue into year 2 (as Security Studies states it).
